last_cycle_outcome: H57 KILL at the prototype rung, ~2.1 h (531.7 s GPU prefix + 9 x ~599 s CPU tails), by a rule sealed and COMMITTED before launch (d3d10ca). THE RESULT THAT OUTLIVES THE ITEM: the champion's relabelling nuisance is created in the SHARED PREFIX, not the refinement tail. Whole-pipeline sigma 0.019124 pp (n=5) vs tail-only sigma 0.003731 pp from one fixed prefix (n=8) - the tail holds ~4% of the variance, the prefix ~96%. So prefix-sharing multiplies R by ~2 while dividing sigma by ~5, and cannot win. New meta-rule M10 generalises that to the whole 'pay the prefix once, randomise the cheap tail' family. THREE GROUNDS, all measured: (1) tail sigma 0.003731 vs an M9 bar of 0.011658 (idle, R=4) / 0.014180 (P07 load, R=3), and unlike H56 it does NOT flip at the chi-squared upper bound 0.007594, which still fails by 35%; (2) the canonical arm is the MAXIMUM of all nine, so canonical-anchored best-of-R gains EXACTLY 0.000000 pp at every R by enumeration, and random-only best-of-4 is -0.010532 pp, a regression; (3) matched compute, the item's own kill condition, prefers ONE longer tail by >= +0.004707 pp. VALIDITY GATE PASSED EXACTLY: prefix reproduced the champion's stage-3 83.91351804242117 and the identity tail its 84.15409511053134. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE RECORD, both stated rather than edited away: the queue item assumed the tail was the expensive half (it is 47%, not ~56%); and THIS CYCLE'S OWN SEALED PREREG wrongly said microns admits R=1 - measured, it is R=3 (prefix 3172.3 s, tail 86.0 s), so H56's runtime ground played no part in this kill. The sealed file was left byte-identical on purpose. FREE RESULT FOR H58: canonical ranked 1 of 9, exchangeability p = 1/9 = 0.111 (quote the rank, not the z of +3.96) - but it points at TIE-BREAK CONSISTENCY between prefix and tail rather than at the on-disk order being special, and the consistency reading predicts no 1x-cost win exists. H58 amended to test that first. sota.json UNTOUCHED; no score moved.

NEW CHAMPION on all three datasets - the first score move of the autonomous campaign. Mechanism: a structural BLOCK move class. Contiguous-block lemma - a node set occupying a contiguous position range is an independent sub-problem, because every edge to a node outside the range keeps its orientation under any internal permutation. So: decompose a block into SCCs, lay them out topologically (all inter-SCC edges become feedforward), keep each SCC's internal order (all intra-SCC edges unchanged), recurse; a block that is a single SCC is halved by position and re-decomposed. Monotone non-decreasing BY CONSTRUCTION, pinned by 31 unit tests. Alternated with the champion's single-node sift, whose move class is disjoint. Confirm (5/5/20 seeds, all bit-identical): connectome 84.097174 (+0.1837 pp vs H35), microns 83.233847 (+0.0276 pp vs H30), mouse 92.917014 (+0.0152 pp). audit exit 0, all 30 runs re-scored exactly. Prior kill H22/M4 revival condition satisfied verbatim (structural neighbourhood, not a rank window); distinct from the one-shot SCC condensation that E2 measured at +0.00013 pp. Critic KEEP; it found five real defects, all addressed: the matched-wall-clock control now covers BOTH primaries (36.0x / 13.0x) and is promoted to experiments/proto_h36_control.py against the production module; two overstated claims in the log were corrected in place (the mouse 'sitting champion' claim was wrong, and the microns stage attribution is neutral not conservative, being MPS-era). Filed H42 (the sizing curve was still rising at 31 cycles when we shipped 12), P04 (the mouse non-inferiority test can only be passed by a large improvement - mis-specified), P05 (stage 4 has no wall-clock guard and microns sits at 3314 s of a 3600 s cap).

NEW CHAMPION x3, second score move of the campaign, from two constants. Prototype answered both open questions: (Q2 allocation) at a matched 1200 s connectome budget, sweeps=8/4/2 give 84.1333/84.1353/84.1588, so the cheap inner sift is worth +0.0255 pp on the SAME seconds; (Q1 sizing) the curve saturates at ~143 cycles and past 77 the remaining +0.0047 pp is below the 0.012 pp minimum effect size, which is why 77 ships. THREE THINGS FOR THE NEXT CYCLE. (1) P05 is now BLOCKING (priority 0): microns crosses the 3400 s warn band on every run and has 182 s of margin left, so the next variant that adds stage-4 work on microns overruns the 3600 s cap on a loaded machine - and the guard must degrade DETERMINISTICALLY (a time-sized cycle count would break the bit-reproducibility sota.json and the P02 1-seed screen rest on). (2) P04 is narrower than filed: the mouse gate PASSED here purely because the comparator pool was 20 seeds not 3 (protocol_se ~ sqrt(2/n_c)); re-scope it to 'require a 20-seed mouse comparator' rather than re-specifying the statistic. (3) New item P06: results/*.json discards history.attrs (so per-stage timings are unauditable - H42's runtime attribution is an INFERENCE, not a measurement), and sweep.sh --role confirm ignores campaign.yaml confirm_seeds and silently defaults to 3 seeds. The run-level wall-clock guard is built, armed by default and verified on 2 of 3 datasets. No algorithm changed; sota.json untouched. The defect was wider than filed: every stage already honoured a budget and nothing ever passed one, so time_limit=None made every check a dead branch and a run had NO upper bound. eval/runtime_guard.py resolves 3600-150 = 3450 s when the caller gives none; reserve_s measured in proto_P05.json (36.0/20.5/0.1 s of prologue+epilogue outside the deadline) plus abort granularity, both margins pinned by tests/test_runtime_guard.py. ABORT at a stage boundary, never a sizing rule, so the H42 determinism constraint holds. Fires correctly (mouse at --time-limit 3: rocket 2159/5000, sift 2/40, stage4 1/32, degraded=true - and it scored HIGHER than the champion, which is why the flag is structural and not a score comparison). Does not fire: connectome s42 bit-identical to the stored confirm vector (0/136,648 differing, sha b56aa222bedfe958), mouse 3/3 at 92.917014. audit.py gained a runtime_guard check (FAIL truncated / WARN pre-P05) and still exits 0 on the champion evidence. Prefix-shared tail multi-start, killed at the prototype rung for ~2.1 h by a pre-registration sealed and committed BEFORE launch (d3d10ca). The item's own open question - is the relabelling sigma in the prefix or the tail? - is answered against it: tail-only sigma 0.003731 pp (n=8, one fixed prefix) vs whole-pipeline 0.019124 pp (n=5), i.e. the prefix makes ~96% of the variance. Three grounds: M9 effect size (bar 0.011658 idle / 0.014180 loaded, and the chi-squared upper bound 0.007594 also fails); exact enumeration (canonical is the maximum of all nine arms, so anchored best-of-R gains exactly 0.000000 pp at every R, and random-only best-of-4 is -0.010532 pp); matched compute (one longer tail buys >= +0.004707 pp). Validity gate passed exactly - the identity arm reproduced 84.15409511053134. New meta-rule M10. Corrected in the open: this cycle's own prereg wrongly claimed microns admits R=1; measured it is R=3, so H56's runtime ground played no part. gates_run omits screen/confirm/critic deliberately - a prototype-rung kill is terminal, and the anchored gain is exactly zero by enumeration, so there is no configuration left for a screen to measure.
